svg.title: Transaction Reverts in the EVM
svg.desc: Shows a Solidity error leading to REVERT, rollback of the failing frame's state and logs, revert data passed to caller, and the difference between a caught child failure, propagated top-level revert, and out-of-gas.
svg.text: Transaction Reverts — Rollback with Failure Data
A failing execution frame rolls back state while returning any remaining gas and revert bytes
Solidity failure path
require / revert / custom error
REVERT (0xfd)
stop current frame
Rollback + return data
state/logs revert in this frame
Failure is caught by parent
• Child state changes and logs roll back.
• Remaining child-frame gas returns.
• Parent checks the failure and continues.
• Parent may finish the whole transaction successfully.
Receipt status depends on the top-level result.
Failure reaches transaction top level
• Top-level execution fails.
• Transaction execution state and logs roll back.
• Included transaction still consumes sender nonce.
• Gas already consumed is still charged.
Receipt status normally equals 0x0.
Revert data can contain
Error(string)
Panic(uint256)
CustomError(args) or arbitrary bytes
A bare revert can return no data.
Payload may be forged by an inner contract.
Normal REVERT ≠ Out-of-Gas
REVERT returns unused frame gas to caller.
Out-of-gas does not return remaining frame gas.
Both roll back state changes in the failing frame.
Insufficient intrinsic gas is a pre-execution validity failure.
How to debug a revert
Check transaction input + receipt status → inspect available revert bytes → decode with the correct ABI
Use a trace/debug API or simulation when the receipt alone does not reveal the cause.
Treat revert data as diagnostic data, not proof of which contract originated the failure.
